pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does reading for information mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading to learn something new
   B. Reading the page numbers
   C. Reading without understanding
   D. Reading only for fun

2. Which word in this sentence is singular: The seller has an onion and two cabbages? (1 mark)
   A. two
   B. cabbages
   C. onion
   D. seller has

3. What is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A type of poem
   B. A list of names
   C. A story about animals
   D. Words that tell someone what to do

4. Where should commas go in: We planted maize beans peas and kale? (1 mark)
   A. After maize and beans
   B. After planted
   C. After kale
   D. After We

5. Which question word asks for a reason? (1 mark)
   A. When
   B. Why
   C. Where
   D. Who

6. Which habit helps you listen well? (1 mark)
   A. Playing with a pencil
   B. Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   C. Looking at the floor
   D. Talking to a neighbour

7. Which is the best first step to find the meaning of a new word in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the whole page
   B. Read the words around it for clues
   C. Ask nobody
   D. Tear the page

8. What does inferring meaning mean? (1 mark)
   A. Copying words
   B. Working out meaning from clues
   C. Spelling backwards
   D. Ignoring the word

9. Where can a class publish its final paragraphs? (1 mark)
   A. In a school or class magazine
   B. Under a bed
   C. On a stone
   D. In the dustbin

10. What does pronunciation mean? (1 mark)
   A. The way we say the sounds of words
   B. The way we write words
   C. The length of a story
   D. The meaning of a word

11. What does the English proverb Look before you leap teach? (1 mark)
   A. Jump quickly
   B. Look at the floor
   C. Never move
   D. Think before you act

12. How can you find the meaning of a new word in a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Tear the page
   B. Ask no one
   C. Ignore it always
   D. Use the context and check a dictionary

13. Why should you plan before writing a story? (1 mark)
   A. To finish early
   B. To organise your ideas
   C. To make it longer
   D. To avoid a title

14. Which sentence uses when correctly? (1 mark)
   A. When we ran home rained it.
   B. When it rained, we ran home.
   C. We when ran.
   D. Rained we when home.

15. What is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   B. A sentence with one word
   C. A list
   D. A title

16. What should you do while listening to instructions about where to place objects? (1 mark)
   A. Look away
   B. Move immediately
   C. Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   D. Talk

17. What is a mosaic? (1 mark)
   A. A picture made of small pieces
   B. A heavy load
   C. A long story
   D. A kind of song

18. What is spoken word? (1 mark)
   A. A silent song
   B. Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   C. A dictionary
   D. A kind of drawing

19. In choral recitation, the group (1 mark)
   A. writes the poem
   B. reads silently
   C. says the poem together at the same pace
   D. sings only

20. What does pace mean when reading a poem? (1 mark)
   A. How fast or slow you read
   B. How long the poem is
   C. How many words rhyme
   D. How loud you read

21. What should you do first when studying a picture for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the whole picture
   B. Copy a story
   C. Write the ending
   D. Cover it

22. Which is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   B. It repeats the title
   C. It has no meaning
   D. It begins a new topic

23. What is community service? (1 mark)
   A. Selling goods
   B. Playing only
   C. Sleeping
   D. Helping the community without pay

24. Why are interjections used more in speech than in formal writing? (1 mark)
   A. They are difficult
   B. They are illegal in writing
   C. They show quick feelings in speech
   D. They are long

25. What can you use to make a poster advert? (1 mark)
   A. A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   B. A blank page
   C. Only a number
   D. Only a full stop

26. Which of these is an adjective in Fresh sweet oranges? (1 mark)
   A. oranges
   B. for
   C. sale
   D. sweet

27. Which is a common field on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Colour of the wall
   B. Type of soil
   C. The number of windows
   D. Name

28. What does format mean for a form? (1 mark)
   A. What it costs
   B. Who wrote it
   C. How old it is
   D. How it is arranged on the page

29. What is a talking object used for? (1 mark)
   A. To show who may speak
   B. To play with
   C. To throw
   D. To hide

30. What does a red eight-sided road sign tell drivers? (1 mark)
   A. Go faster
   B. Turn left
   C. Stop
   D. Park

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Put the steps in order: (a) Finally, serve. (b) First, boil water. (c) Next, add tea leaves. (3 marks)

32. Explain how to work out the meaning of an unknown word using context. (4 marks)

33. Write a paragraph of four sentences about a time you handled money. Use when at least twice. (5 marks)

34. Explain what a form is. (2 marks)

35. Describe how a group can read a text aloud together and give feedback. (4 marks)

36. Write one instruction from the road safety dialogue. (2 marks)

37. Rewrite correctly: we live in nairobi (2 marks)

38. Explain what an interjection is and give two examples. (2 marks)

39. Explain how the position game is played with objects on a table. (4 marks)

40. Compose a four-line poem about a good leader. Make lines two and four rhyme. (4 marks)

41. Name two elements of a story. (2 marks)

42. Explain what turn taking means. (2 marks)

43. Explain why leaders are important and why people should obey fair leaders. Give two examples of leaders in a community. (5 marks)

44. Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion. (2 marks)

45. Write a five-line role play dialogue on personal safety between a child and a stranger. Show the speaker names and use question marks correctly. (5 marks)

46. What is a conjunction? Give one example. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Reading to learn something new
   We read for information to find facts and learn.

2. C — onion
   Onion names one thing. Cabbages is plural.

3. D — Words that tell someone what to do
   An instruction says what to do.

4. A — After maize and beans
   The list is maize, beans, peas and kale.

5. B — Why
   Why asks the reason.

6. B — Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   You can follow better when you see and hear clearly.

7. B — Read the words around it for clues
   Context clues are the words nearby.

8. B — Working out meaning from clues
   Inferring uses clues in the context.

9. A — In a school or class magazine
   Publishing shares the writing.

10. A — The way we say the sounds of words
   Pronunciation is how words are said.

11. D — Think before you act
   It advises careful thought before doing something.

12. D — Use the context and check a dictionary
   Context clues and a dictionary help.

13. B — To organise your ideas
   A plan gives your story a clear shape.

14. B — When it rained, we ran home.
   It shows two events joined by time.

15. A — Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   It joins two ideas.

16. C — Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   Full listening avoids mistakes.

17. A — A picture made of small pieces
   A mosaic is made of small pieces of paper or seeds.

18. B — Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   Spoken word is performed poetry.

19. C — says the poem together at the same pace
   Choral means together.

20. A — How fast or slow you read
   Pace is speed.

21. A — Look at the whole picture
   First see the whole picture.

22. A — It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

23. D — Helping the community without pay
   Community service benefits others.

24. C — They show quick feelings in speech
   Formal writing usually uses full sentences.

25. A — A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   Adverts have these parts.

26. D — sweet
   Sweet describes the oranges.

27. D — Name
   Name is a common field.

28. D — How it is arranged on the page
   Format is the layout.

29. A — To show who may speak
   Only the holder speaks.

30. C — Stop
   That shape is the stop sign.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: b, c, a
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct position.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the sentence with the word, look at nearby words for clues, guess a meaning, check that it makes sense in the sentence and confirm in a dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two uses of when, for example When I reached the shop, I counted my money. When I paid, I received change. I was happy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear sentence and one mark for correct use of when.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form is a page with spaces where people write information in an organised way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a page with spaces and one for collecting information.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, help each other with hard words, take turns to read, then listen to the group and give one good point and one point to improve in a kind way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct parts.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look right, then left, then right again. (or Cross at a zebra crossing.)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a correct instruction and one for a complete sentence.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: We live in Nairobi.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capital letters and one for the full stop.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: An interjection is a short word or sound showing sudden feeling, for example Wow and Ouch.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for two examples.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: One pupil gives an instruction such as put the pencil on the book. Another follows it. The class checks whether the position is correct. Then the roles are swapped.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on leadership with two rhyming lines, for example A good leader listens, Speaks the truth each day, Helps the weak and lonely, And shows the proper way.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme and four lines, two marks for rhyme.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means speaking one person at a time and waiting for others to finish before speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for one at a time and one for waiting.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Leaders guide, make decisions and keep order. Obeying fair leaders keeps peace and safety. Examples: chief, teacher, class monitor, elders.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for why leaders are important, two marks for obeying and one for examples.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: cabbages, onions
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five correct lines, for example Child: Good afternoon. Stranger: Do you want a ride? Child: No, thank you. I will wait for my mother. Stranger: Are you sure? Child: Yes, I am telling my teacher.
   Working / marking points: One mark for speaker names, one for a safe message, one for correct questions and two for five clear lines.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: A conjunction is a joining word, such as and, but or when.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for an example.
